In one sentence: the matrix geometric mean can jump at singular matrices, every possible jump is described by one rank condition, and the same mechanism refutes a published claim that the symbol of the geometric mean of two GLT matrix-sequences is always the geometric mean of their symbols. The geometric mean A#B of two positive definite matrices is the matrix analogue of √(ab), used to average covariance matrices and structured matrices and to define the Matsumoto fidelity of quantum states. It need not be continuous at singular pairs. Theorem 1 shows that X is a limit of A j #B j with positive definite A j → A, B j → B exactly when X ≽ 0, the block matrix [[A, X], [X, B]] is positive semidefinite and its rank is at most the dimension N (a dilation description with an auxiliary contraction already follows from recent work of Jones; the explicit elimination is the contribution). At equal inputs this gives the full set of limits and the exact interval of limiting Matsumoto fidelities. For generalized locally Toeplitz (GLT) matrix-sequences, uniformly bounded positive definite inputs with identical scalar symbols can have geometric means with the wrong symbol (4/5 instead of 1 on half the interval) or no eigenvalue distribution at all. This refutes Theorem 4 and Conjecture 1 of the arXiv version of Ilyas, Khan, Loi and Serra-Capizzano and, according to an AI-assisted reading of the published text, Theorem 3 and Conjecture 1 of their article in Linear Algebra Appl. (2025); the failing step of the proof is located. Positive results: closure for every Kubo-Ando mean when the sum of the symbols is positive definite almost everywhere; a one-sided theorem that the regularised symbol is always an upper envelope; and, for bounded Riemann-integrable scalar symbols of the space variable only, a sharp dichotomy (the formula holds for every realisation if and only if the symbols have no common zero set of positive measure or essentially disjoint supports). The classical two-dimensional discontinuity, Ando's maximal characterisation and the envelope X ≼ A#B are earlier work and are credited. The archive contains the manuscript (PDF and Markdown source), two figures with the script that draws them, an exact verifier (verify_exact.py, Python standard library only, 1,030 rational and Gaussian-rational checks of closed forms and finite assemblies, with a mutation self-test) and its retained output, the bibliography with its Crossref/arXiv records, the dated novelty ledger, a revision note, CI and SHA-256 sums. Assurance: written proofs; the verifier checks finite exact identities, not the theorems' limits or quantifiers; internal AI-assisted review only (not human peer review, independent reproduction or formal verification). items.summary: We disprove a three-step error estimate for the Broyden--Fletcher--Goldfarb--Shanno {(BFGS)} method with exact line searches. We construct a globally strongly convex function $F\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$ and a single nonterminating trajectory $x_k\to0$ for which $\limsup_{k\to\infty}\|x_{k+3}\|/(\|x_{k+2}\|\|x_k\|)=+\infty$. The Hessian of $F$ lies between $\tfrac12 I$ and $\tfrac32 I$ everywhere, and $F(x)-\tfrac12\|x\|^2$ is compactly supported with all derivatives vanishing at $0$. The proof first constructs point-gradient pairs satisfying the exact BFGS step identities. A five-step cycle produces a large three-step quotient and restores an invariant plane for the actual updated matrix, allowing the cycle to be repeated with arbitrarily small gradient errors. Disjoint smooth corrections to a quadratic then realize all the pairs by one objective. Strong convexity identifies the prescribed points with the unique exact line-search minimizers. Thus smoothness and strong convexity do not imply the proposed product estimate, even for an objective that agrees with a quadratic to every order at its minimizer.
items.title: A counterexample to a three-step convergence bound for BFGS with exact line search

items.summary: Support points provide a practical and effective way to approximate a probability distribution by a small set of equally weighted representatives through energy-distance minimization. In many applications, the variables satisfy convex constraints that the representatives should also respect. We investigate whether unconstrained support points automatically satisfy such constraints and show that this is not guaranteed. We construct counterexamples using three planar observations, a density with full triangular support, and positive-definite matrix data admitting an indefinite optimal representative under the Frobenius norm. We also identify cases in which containment holds, establish stability under distributional perturbations, and quantify the objective cost of imposing a convex-hull constraint. For a fixed number of representatives and a positive population constraint gap, empirical configurations with vanishing global objective error eventually leave the sample convex hull almost surely.
items.title: Unconstrained support points can leave a convex support

items.summary: We give a negative answer to a question of Sánchez Saldaña--Velásquez and Lück asking whether the topological K-theory of the reduced group C*-algebra of a split crystallographic group with finite cyclic holonomy is always torsion-free. For two explicit split crystallographic groups with translation subgroup of rank four and holonomy of order four, we compute the equivariant K-theory of the classifying space for proper actions and find nontrivial two-torsion. The equivariant universal coefficient theorem transfers this torsion to proper equivariant K-homology, and the Baum--Connes conjecture identifies the resulting groups with the topological K-theory of the corresponding reduced group C*-algebras.
items.title: Counterexamples to torsion-freeness in the $K$-theory of crystallographic group $C^*$-algebras

items.summary: Overview: This deposit hosts the official replication package, synthetic benchmark dataset, and experimental audit artifacts for the scientific manuscript: "M-11: Auditing Synthetic Risk Labels and Physical Baselines in a Cyber-Physical Benchmark for Underground Mining" (submitted to Acta Montanistica Slovaca , 2026). M-11 is a simulation-only cyber-physical benchmark that integrates AI4I 2020 predictive maintenance attributes with synthetic kinematic positioning, physiological, and environmental indicators (10,000 records; 37 columns) to audit the statistical mechanics and potential circularity of synthetic risk labelling in confined underground mining operations. Key Empirical Findings Reported in the Manuscript: Label Circularity Audit: Variance decomposition demonstrates that 82.07% of the synthetic score variance is driven by spatial/kinematic components, 17.43% by injected noise, 0.48% by multimodal variables, and 0.02% by cross-covariance. Symmetric Holdout Evaluation (n = 2,000; seed 42): Calibrated Time-to-Collision (TTC) and Random Forest both achieve F2 = 0.9103; XGBoost achieves F2 = 0.9065. The paired bootstrap difference (ΔF2 = -0.0038, 95% CI: -0.0129 to 0.0047) and Holm-adjusted McNemar test (p = 0.6015) confirm no statistically significant gap under circular labels. Decoupled Hazard Stress Tests: Under 22% class prevalence and low signal-to-noise ratio, non-spatial decoupled labels (CO, fatigue, vibration) push F2 optimisation to near-universal HIGH alerts, approaching the trivial Always-HIGH baseline (F2 = 0.5851). A multimodal-only composite target recovers F2 = 0.6408 with 54.1% specificity. Feature Ablations: Removing three direct kinematic indicators reduces F2 by 9.60 percentage points; removing the entire 8-feature spatial block reduces F2 by 32.52 percentage points from the full 0.9065 baseline. Computational Scalability: Local backend P95 latency scales to 27.91 ms under 500 concurrent simulated agents (< 200 ms supervisory threshold). The WebGL/Three.js integrated-GPU prototype achieves 34.8 FPS under nominal load. Deterministic Safety & GenAI Audit: The independent deterministic safety layer satisfies 17 automated unit/integration tests and 100/100 scripted regulatory scenario checks. The Gemini language model acts strictly as an exploratory natural-language interface without numerical autonomy. items.summary: The Sundarbans mangrove system constitutes a globally consequential blue carbon sink, yet vertically resolved soil organic carbon (SOC) inventories, particularly at depth, remain under-constrained. This study deployed a geospatial deep-learning pipeline integrating multi-source Earth observation data (optical, SAR, and DEM-derived covariates) to spatially upscale SOC stocks to 1 m depth across the Bangladesh Sundarbans. Stratified coring across five sites positioned along the salinity–tidal inundation gradient to represent four major vegetation zones (n = 25; one pit per site × five depth intervals: 0–20, 20–40, 40–60, 60–80, 80–100 cm) captured physicochemical and SOC attributions. A Kruskal–Wallis test confirmed a positive SOC gradient with depth (H = 21.7, df = 4, p < 0.001); post-hoc Dunn’s pairwise comparisons showed 60–100 cm layers differed significantly from all shallower layers (p < 0.01, Bonferroni-adjusted), with the dominant pool residing below 40 cm, implying systematic underestimation by conventional shallow-core (<30–40 cm) assessments. To partition total ecosystem carbon and establish soil-pool dominance, above- and belowground biomass were parameterized using species-specific allometric equations, revealing high stem density but comparatively low basal area consistent with a regenerating stand structure dominated by Heritiera fomes and Sonneratia apetala. Analysis of a previously published Landsat-derived mangrove record (1988–2022) revealed net contraction in mangrove extent; loss-agent raster attribution, based on shoreline-proximity buffers, land-cover transition sequences and cyclone-track coincidence, identified chronic tidal abrasion and erosion as the primary driver rather than anthropogenic conversion or cyclonic disturbance. Benchmarking against a previously published global 30 m machine-learning SOC product revealed a 4.2-fold underestimation of SOC stocks in the Bangladesh Sundarbans, particularly in peat-enriched, anoxic substrata. Assimilation of deep-profile in situ observations with the pipeline significantly improves spatial prediction fidelity and establishes a robust baseline for Measurement, Reporting, and Verification for greenhouse gas inventories, highlighting the necessity of incorporating deep-soil carbon pools for inventorizing erosion-vulnerable seaward margins.
items.title: Blue Carbon Stock Mapping of the Sundarbans Mangrove Ecosystem, Bangladesh (2000–2025): A Hybrid GeoAI Ensemble Framework

items.summary: Measured failure modes of verifier panels: companion paper accepted (poster) at the NeurIPS 2026 workshop Who Verifies the Agents? — Verification Theater: Measured Failure Modes of AI Verifier Panels . Version of record: SSRN 7390698 , DOI 10.2139/ssrn.7390698 . Cite that version. The same text is also at https://polyhelper.ai/research/agreement-not-evidence/ and https://github.com/vadimchernets/papers/tree/main/agreement-not-evidence . Someone who asks one language model a question cannot tell a confidently wrong answer from a confidently right one. The two are identical on every surface cue available to a non-expert. Asking several models seems to solve this, but it mostly relocates the problem: reconciling several answers produces one confident text again, and that text now carries the borrowed authority of "ten of them agreed." The protocol formalized here collects answers from several consumer chat models through the user's own browser or phone, with no API keys, no installation and no intermediary server. It reconciles them by anchor-and-enrich: the strongest available answer becomes the base, and each of the others contributes only what the base lacks. Every contribution is signed with the model that supplied it. Disagreements are kept in a section of their own rather than averaged away. The paper makes four contributions. The first is the protocol itself, stated as an algorithm that preserves provenance and forbids silent deletion, together with a taxonomy of five ways a merge can fail. Four of them are defects of naive pooling; the fifth is a failure of the operator rather than of the method: a synthesis that presents a single model's output as a collegial result. The second is the application of the correlated-witness arithmetic to protocol design. That arithmetic is not claimed here. Kohli (2026) applied the same Kish correction to a panel of nine frontier judges and measured about two effective votes, and Kim et al. (2025) established the underlying error correlation across more than 350 models. A council of N models whose errors carry intraclass correlation ρ is worth = N / (1 + (N−1)ρ) independent witnesses, and that quantity saturates at 1/ρ however many models are added. Once a council is larger than 1/ρ, halving ρ beats doubling N, and a pair with low error correlation can outweigh five with high correlation. Which pairs those are is measured, not read off the label: the larger and more accurate models carry the most correlated errors even when architecture and provider differ (Kim et al., 2025), and the author's per-pair measurements found no detectable effect of geopolitical bloc on error correlation and, in the pairs measured, none of shared lineage (Chernets, 2026). The estimation procedure of Section 5.5 supplies that measurement. The third is an account of three deployment tiers, manual, one-tap mobile and browser-agent, and of the axis that separates them epistemically: whether the second model sees the first model's answer. Conditioning the second model raises ρ in exchange for error correction. The fourth is a small-sample observation of the counterfeit-council failure across five models, the one-sentence intervention that removed it in a three-model re-run, and a blinded three-arm evaluation design with a stated falsification condition. Correlated agreement is treated here as established, not as a finding. That a panel of models is worth far fewer independent witnesses than it has members has been measured directly: nine frontier judges drawn from seven families supply about two effective votes (Kohli, 2026), and error correlation rises with model capability even across providers and architectures (Kim et al., 2025). Section 5 restates the design-effect arithmetic behind those measurements, because three of the protocol's rules are derived from it and read as fastidiousness without it. items.summary: Unrefereed research candidate. In one sentence: identical Kuramoto oscillators scattered at random on a flat torus of any fixed dimension have stable twisted equilibria near every integer winding, which proves the twisted-equilibrium conjecture of Cirelli, Groisman, Huang and Vivas for every kernel in their class with |z|K(z) bounded. Place n identical oscillators at independent uniform points of the flat torus T d and couple points closer than ε n with weight K(z/ε n ). If ε n → 0 and nε n d+2 /log n → ∞, then with high probability, for every integer twist k with |k| ≤ c/(ε n +δ n ), where δ n = (log n/(nε n d+2 )) 1/2 , there is an asymptotically stable equilibrium whose phase differs from k·x by at most C|k|δ n at every vertex (Theorem 2.1). The kernel need only be even, supported in the unit ball, positive almost everywhere near the origin and have sup|z|K(z) finite: this covers the hard-radius graph, every bounded kernel and |z| −α , 0 < α ≤ 1. All twists k in Z d are covered, not only coordinate twists. Further results: at least c(ε n +δ n ) −d distinct stable constructed states; a basin of fixed size; for bounded radial kernels, a heat-equation limit uniform over all times; and stable weighted harmonic lifts under smooth nonuniform sampling (bounded kernels). The key tool is a sup-norm bound for the inverse graph Laplacian uniform over all conductances above a bounded backbone. The archive contains the manuscript (PDF and LaTeX source), an exact standard-library checker of classical cycle twisted-state spectra, the numerical illustrations with their script and records, verification and claim records, preserved development drafts, two unrelated supplementary research notes kept for provenance, a rating-free internal review summary, CI and SHA-256 sums. Assurance: written informal proofs; internal AI-agent review and proof audits only (not peer review, independent reproduction or formal verification); kernels with |z|K unbounded and the connectivity regime nε d ~ log n remain open; constants are not explicit; the numerics are small illustrations outside the theorem's regime. items.summary: Abstract Sānér establishes a recursive control architecture for task regions by placing topology, self-modeling scheduling, and certificate-governed execution under one executable resource semantics. The nine-node construction supports exact recursive expansion and addressing. Its formal system establishes capacity safety, deterministic cross-layer selection, partition safety, conditional liveness, and computable deadline and recovery bounds. Using entity-isolated validation and one-time test splits, we evaluated the shared kernels and domain adapters in executable state-transition simulations and public benchmark workloads over 32–64 independent worlds, with deployment evidence obtained from 48 physical GPU blocks and eight fresh process pairs in the official Kubernetes scheduler-performance harness. Shared kernels with explicit domain realizations established task-level all-comparator superiority, while matched Kubernetes execution established a throughput advantage over the official default scheduler. The recursive representation preserved exact adjacency with a small measured footprint as graph size increased. Mechanism evidence remains separate from direct performance claims. Boundary results and nonidentifiability tests are reported independently. Together, the proofs and matched comparisons establish Sānér as a reusable and auditable control architecture whose shared mechanisms transfer across structurally different systems tasks. Validation design The study reports 52 simulation tasks and two deployment endpoints. Simulation comparisons use matched frozen worlds, observable information, action spaces, resource ceilings, and decision-time budgets. The Kubernetes deployment uses fresh paired processes under the same official scheduling and binding boundaries. items.summary: Rapid advances in cowork agents are shifting human-AI collaboration toward real-world automation, delivering software, designs, and other artifacts. However, such productivity work demands both high-quality delivery on complex productivity tasks and continued monitoring and decision-making over long horizons, a combination that remains an open challenge. We introduce CoworkOS, a general-purpose harness for long-horizon work that separates task strategy from execution management: the model decides actions, delegation, and acceptance, while the runtime maintains state and feedback. Its three-layer architecture enables direct execution or delegation to Subagents, synchronously or asynchronously, under stable responsibilities. Through a shared application layer, humans and agents inspect and revise the same evolving documents, presentations, CAD models, and Blender scenes, so human-in-the-loop participation can enter both through conversation and through direct modification of the work itself. To sustain continuity across agents and sessions, CoworkOS further introduces hierarchical workspaces and persistent semantic memory, so working files, key decisions, and long-running Job logs remain shareable, reusable, and resumable after interruption. Across 12 benchmarks and 6 categories of real-world applications, CoworkOS proves highly competitive with frontier agent applications such as Codex and DeepSeek Harness. As a sustained-work case study, CoworkOS uses GLM-5.3 as its backbone to conduct RSI-driven automated post-training on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B. Over five rounds, the model's average score across eight benchmarks rose from 33.19 to 42.95 (+9.76). Looking ahead, we believe CoworkOS opens a meaningful path toward general cowork-agent intelligence.
items.title: CoworkOS:Scaling Agent Coworkers for Real-world Automation

items.summary: Full Waveform Inversion (FWI) is a fundamental inverse problem in geophysics to estimate subsurface properties, such as velocity, from seismic measurements. Recently, self-supervised learning methods remove the need for ground-truth velocity maps during training by leveraging a forward operator to simulate seismic data from predictions and backpropagate the gradients of reconstruction loss through it. In this work, we consider a more challenging setting without accessing such gradients. To this end, we incorporate reinforcement learning into self-supervised FWI and propose a framework named DeepWaveRL. Specifically, we reformulate FWI as a policy learning problem, where the policy network predicts velocity maps as actions, and a forward operator is used solely for simulation. A global scalar reward is computed based on data misfit for each prediction and used to weight policy gradients. Thus, learning proceeds without accessing the gradients from the forward operator. Given the indirect and coarse supervision signals, we further identify key strategies to stabilize learning and mitigate the spatial credit assignment bottleneck. Experimental results show that, despite relying entirely on a single scalar reward, DeepWaveRL achieves competitive performance compared to supervised and self-supervised baselines. These findings suggest that our framework offers a flexible and complementary learning paradigm for the FWI research community.
items.title: DeepWaveRL: Self-Supervised Full Waveform Inversion via Reinforcement Learning

In one sentence: identical Kuramoto oscillators scattered at random on a flat torus of any fixed dimension have stable twisted equilibria near every integer winding, which proves the twisted-equilibrium conjecture of Cirelli, Groisman, Huang and Vivas for every kernel in their class with |z|K(z) bounded. Place n identical oscillators at independent uniform points of the flat torus T d and couple points closer than ε n with weight K(z/ε n ). If ε n → 0 and nε n d+2 /log n → ∞, then with high probability, for every integer twist k with |k| ≤ c/(ε n +δ n ), where δ n = (log n/(nε n d+2 )) 1/2 , there is an asymptotically stable equilibrium whose phase differs from k·x by at most C|k|δ n at every vertex (Theorem 2.1). The kernel need only be even, supported in the unit ball, positive almost everywhere near the origin and have sup|z|K(z) finite: this covers the hard-radius graph, every bounded kernel and |z| −α , 0 < α ≤ 1. All twists k in Z d are covered, not only coordinate twists. Further results: at least c(ε n +δ n ) −d distinct stable constructed states; a basin of fixed size; for bounded radial kernels, a heat-equation limit uniform over all times; and stable weighted harmonic lifts under smooth nonuniform sampling (bounded kernels). The key tool is a sup-norm bound for the inverse graph Laplacian uniform over all conductances above a bounded backbone. The archive contains the manuscript (PDF and LaTeX source), an exact standard-library checker of classical cycle twisted-state spectra, the numerical illustrations with their script and records, verification and claim records, preserved development drafts, two unrelated supplementary research notes kept for provenance, a rating-free internal review summary, CI and SHA-256 sums. Assurance: written informal proofs; internal AI-agent review and proof audits only (not peer review, independent reproduction or formal verification); kernels with |z|K unbounded and the connectivity regime nε d ~ log n remain open; constants are not explicit; the numerics are small illustrations outside the theorem's regime. items.summary: High-dimensional data from multiple sources often combine shared structure with source-specific variation. We study heterogeneous principal component analysis, which seeks to recover common and private principal subspaces when their dimensions are unknown. {We propose \emph{Feature Extraction (FE)}, a novel data-driven framework with two steps. First, the Eigenvector-based Spike-Count (ESC) estimator determines the number of principal components (PC) in each source using only sample eigenvector information, rather than eigenvalue-based criteria. Second, FE identifies the locations of common features by comparing bias-corrected inner products between sample eigenvectors across sources. These matches yield estimates of the common and source-specific subspaces without iterative optimization. We establish the consistency of our estimators under a spiked covariance model in a high-dimensional regime where the dimension and sample size grow proportionally. Simulations and applications to federated image data and U.S. housing prices demonstrate the performance of FE in rank recovery, subspace estimation, and data reconstruction.} Code is available at https://github.com/liwenbo-research/HeterogeneousPCA

items.summary: Interactive world generation requires both accurate local control and stable scene consistency over long rollouts. Existing methods improve local generation through camera or geometry conditioning and extend historical context with memory mechanisms. However, long-horizon exploration remains challenging as target-view guidance becomes incomplete and inconsistencies accumulate across repeated scene updates. We present \textbf{GSExplorer}, a generation--reconstruction framework built around a persistent 3D Gaussian world state. At each step, the current 3DGS scene provides multimodal rendering conditions for a condition-driven video generator, while camera geometry is injected through a separate Relative Ray Encoding branch. Generated videos are then fed back to a SLAM-based reconstruction backend, where inconsistency filtering prevents conflicting content from corrupting the scene and cross-chunk bundle adjustment improves spatial alignment across generation steps. We further design a data-construction pipeline that reproduces realistic 3DGS degradation during scene extrapolation, yielding 293K training pairs of degraded multimodal renderings and real target videos. GSExplorer achieves the best overall performance among the compared methods on both single-step and three-step WorldScore evaluation, with strong camera control and consistency across both settings, including a Camera Control score of 99.07 in single-step extrapolation. On 481-frame leave-and-return rollouts, it also shows strong revisit consistency, demonstrating the value of maintaining a reliable 3D world state for continued exploration.

items.summary: A provenance-bound values model published as a public evaluator rather than deployed as a filter — why open weights defeat a filter and strengthen a referee, why the same weights bear three different relations to the model they judge, and why an evaluator that gatekeeps its own judgments has reproduced the defect it exists to correct. A values model — a model that judges conduct against a standard — is an established artifact. Guard models, safety classifiers, critic models, preference models and process reward models all instantiate the family, and the engineering is not in dispute. What is in dispute, and what this paper specifies, is the posture in which such an artifact is published , which we argue is not a deployment detail but the property that determines whether the artifact does anything at all. We state an inversion as a design principle. A values model deployed as a filter — sitting in a serving path, permitting or refusing — is defeated by publication of its weights, because the published artifact is precisely the oracle against which an attacker optimizes; a staged black-box attack (STACK) reaches roughly 71% success against a defended classifier pipeline that had held earlier attacks near zero, and an attacker holding the weights has strictly more than that attack needed. The same model published as an evaluator — emitting verdicts about systems it does not control — is not defeated by publication, and its positive findings are strengthened by it, because open weights are what allow a third party to reproduce and therefore to trust its verdicts. The same openness hands the judged party an optimization target, and §4.1 states what that concedes: a clean or empty result from an open referee proves less against an adaptive party than the first draft of this paper allowed. Openness is not a property with a fixed sign. Its sign is set by posture, and in the referee posture it is mixed. From this we derive a second result. The independent-evaluation literature documents at length the ways in which the evaluated party's control over access corrupts evaluation: short access windows, low rate limits, evaluator dependence on the goodwill and funding of the party being evaluated. We observe that the defect is symmetric and that, in the work surveyed in §2, its mirror image has not been named. An evaluator that controls access to its own judgments holds the same kind of power, pointed the other way — it can decline to evaluate, deprioritize, or be unavailable for a party it wishes to spare or to punish. We therefore specify a non-gatekeeping constraint : the ability to obtain a judgment must not depend on the evaluator's permission, which requires that the model, the harness, and the evaluation corpus be freely runnable, and which makes any hosted endpoint a convenience rather than a channel. We specify provenance-binding as the constitutive constraint on the model's outputs: every judgment must resolve to a citation into a fixed canonical corpus, and a judgment that cannot be so resolved is withheld rather than emitted. This trades coverage for auditability deliberately, and it distinguishes the artifact from values models trained on preference data whose sources cannot be named, and from purpose-authored value-rule corpora, whose rules are written for the alignment task itself and therefore cannot serve as an independent ground truth. Finally we specify that a single such artifact bears three non-interchangeable relations to the systems it judges, selected by carrier: a gate in the publisher's own hardware, a citation requirement without veto in an autonomous successor agent, and a referee in the wider world. We state plainly that the middle case must not be implemented as the first, because a veto held by a smaller model over a more capable agent bounds that agent at the evaluator's ceiling — the weak-supervisor problem applied to the very system the arrangement exists to enable. items.summary: Measured failure modes of verifier panels: companion paper accepted (poster) at the NeurIPS 2026 workshop Who Verifies the Agents? — Verification Theater: Measured Failure Modes of AI Verifier Panels . Version of record: SSRN 7390698 , DOI 10.2139/ssrn.7390698 . Cite that version. The same text is also at https://polyhelper.ai/research/agreement-not-evidence/ and https://github.com/vadimchernets/papers/tree/main/agreement-not-evidence . Someone who asks one language model a question cannot tell a confidently wrong answer from a confidently right one. The two are identical on every surface cue available to a non-expert. Asking several models seems to solve this, but it mostly relocates the problem: reconciling several answers produces one confident text again, and that text now carries the borrowed authority of "ten of them agreed." The protocol formalized here collects answers from several consumer chat models through the user's own browser or phone, with no API keys, no installation and no intermediary server. It reconciles them by anchor-and-enrich: the strongest available answer becomes the base, and each of the others contributes only what the base lacks. Every contribution is signed with the model that supplied it. Disagreements are kept in a section of their own rather than averaged away. The paper makes four contributions. The first is the protocol itself, stated as an algorithm that preserves provenance and forbids silent deletion, together with a taxonomy of five ways a merge can fail. Four of them are defects of naive pooling; the fifth is a failure of the operator rather than of the method: a synthesis that presents a single model's output as a collegial result. The second is the application of the correlated-witness arithmetic to protocol design. That arithmetic is not claimed here. Kohli (2026) applied the same Kish correction to a panel of nine frontier judges and measured about two effective votes, and Kim et al. (2025) established the underlying error correlation across more than 350 models. A council of N models whose errors carry intraclass correlation ρ is worth = N / (1 + (N−1)ρ) independent witnesses, and that quantity saturates at 1/ρ however many models are added. Once a council is larger than 1/ρ, halving ρ beats doubling N, and a pair with low error correlation can outweigh five with high correlation. Which pairs those are is measured, not read off the label: the larger and more accurate models carry the most correlated errors even when architecture and provider differ (Kim et al., 2025), and the author's per-pair measurements found no detectable effect of geopolitical bloc on error correlation and, in the pairs measured, none of shared lineage (Chernets, 2026). The estimation procedure of Section 5.5 supplies that measurement. items.summary: Sensor fusion, data fusion, dashboards and data visualisation are conventionally distinguished by input type and by where they sit in a processing stack. This paper argues that the distinction which matters for decision quality is a different one, and that it is two variables applied to all four: every representation of multi-source evidence collapses a distribution somewhere between sensor and decision, and representations differ in the locus of that collapse and in whether the residual uncertainty survives it as a carried object. Fusion collapses upstream and, when honest, ships the residual as covariance or hypothesis mass. Dashboards defer collapse to the viewer's retina and ship nothing; the resulting belief has no bookkeeping. Visualisation is the encoding of whichever object arrives, indifferent to whether it is a point or a distribution, which is why it is blamed for collapses committed upstream. The two variables, collapse locus and residual retention, place the four terms on one map, generalise the confabulation coefficient of The Confabulating Collator from language-model collators to the whole representation stack, and yield a diagnostic: the failure mode conventionally called bad fusion is a product that collapsed upstream and discarded its residual, delivering the confidence of a posterior with the epistemic hygiene of a gauge. The publicly reported expectation, in the investigation of the February 2026 Minab strike, that a targeting platform would have flagged contradictions it carried no representation of, is read as this failure at operational scale, with the causal question left where the public record leaves it. A design rule follows: defer collapse to the human where the human carries the prior the system lacks, fuse where they do not, and at neither locus discard the residual. The constructive requirement for language-level fusion products is stated and handed to a companion paper on divergence retention. The operator located in the architecture is Binary Bias.

items.summary: Binary Bias (Temte 2026a) claims that the collapse of continuous, conditional and multi-valued phenomena into sealed either/or categories is a substrate from which other catalogued biases grow. The claim has so far been argued, not counted. This paper specifies an audit that counts it: a random sample of 3,000 journal-article abstracts drawn through Crossref's sampling endpoint, enriched with field and era metadata from OpenAlex, and coded for binary collapse by three independent language-model coders with ten percent human double-coding. The coding scheme separates four loci at which a binary can sit (territory, design, inference, format), scores severity on a 0 to 5 Boolikert rather than as present or absent, and counts the sealing of a null result into an absence claim (nulsegl) as its own category. An evening-scale pilot of twenty abstracts, reported in full, motivates six hypotheses with pre-stated effect sizes: that inference- and format-locus collapse appears in at least a quarter of abstracts; that the format locus dominates in clinical literature and the inference locus in social and policy literature; that nulsegl is the single most frequent collapse type; that fields whose core object is already a ratio collapse less than fields whose core object is a category; that the 2016 statement on p-values changed vocabulary rather than verdicts; and that abstracts collapse more than the discussion sections they summarise. Publication of the protocol before the data is the pre-registration; the result is published whichever way it falls.

items.summary: Wave energy converters (WECs) are typically designed to operate near resonance to maximize energy capture. While this enhances power absorption, it also amplifies structural loads and accelerates fatigue damage. As a result, fatigue becomes a critical design driver even when stress remains below material yield limits. Fatigue in offshore systems has been widely studied, particularly under variable-amplitude loading induced by waves, wind, and currents. These effects are commonly evaluated using the Palmgren–Miner damage accumulation rule, where failure is predicted once cumulative damage reaches unity. However, fatigue assessment for WECs remains less developed, especially in terms of linking environmental conditions to structural degradation and operational stress limits. The objective of this work is to evaluate, predict and improve confidence in the structural response and fatigue life of a WEC under representative operating conditions and to identify critical components and failure modes before deployment in March 2026 accounting for not only load and geometric factors, but also environmental conditions such as temperature.

items.summary: Classical creative-process orderings put divergence early and convergence late, and the Double Diamond formalises the rule twice over. This paper argues the ordering was never a law of cognition but a map of costs: divergence goes early because reopening a converged process has historically been ruinous, and the entire discipline of the framework exists to protect against that reopening. When drafting cost collapses by orders of magnitude, as it does when an author works with a language model as typewriter, the protected assumption dissolves and the optimal ordering inverts: converge first, then diverge, because a late horizon either restarts a now-cheap process or spawns a child concept from a sharpened parent. The paper's second claim types reviewer instances in multi-model chains by regression target rather than capability, and states the Hein Condition: a mode-regressing reviewer's yield is proportional to the sharpness of the artefact it receives, because the modal response to an unsharp artefact is the generic response, so the same instance is most fluent exactly where it is least useful. A slot theory follows, carnivore, auditor, mode-regressor, children, each reviewer placed where its failure mode is cheapest, and child viability rises with parent sharpness at spawn. The claims are exercised on a fully documented case: a five-pass, three-model review chain run on a single paper in a single day, with every absorption, declination, and provenance failure logged. Four predictions close, including that review chains are provenance systems measurable by the sibling paper's key-inflation ratio.

items.summary: Abstract: Keeping the modern power grid running during heatwaves, wildfires, or cyberattacks requires knowing which power lines are the most dangerous "dominoes" if two or three of them fail at the same time. However, checking every possible combination of multiple broken lines across the Western U.S. grid is a math problem with millions of possibilities—far too slow for computers to solve in real time using standard physics equations. Conversely, taking shortcuts by simply looking at a map of the grid (to find the biggest, most connected hubs) fails because electricity does not travel like cars on a highway; it cannot be told which road to take. Instead, electricity automatically splits across all available wires based on their physical resistance. When a major line gets crowded or breaks, electricity surges onto smaller side-lines, causing chain-reaction blackouts far away from the original problem. In this memo, we introduce Physics-Informed Network Reshaping (PINR), an AI framework that bridges the gap between map-based speed and physical accuracy. PINR combines a specialized, mathematically predictable neural network with a network-disruption algorithm originally designed for counter-terrorism. Rather than testing millions of broken-wire combinations one by one, PINR uses a single, rapid pass to act as a dual-use stress gauge: For Grid Defenders ("Blue Team" Healing): It shows grid operators the exact 27 congested power lines where slightly "throttling" the flow (like adjusting valves on a water pipe) relieves 99.1% of grid overloads during a peak evening crunch, pushing excess electricity safely onto underused backup lines. For Security Analysts ("Red Team" Vulnerability Hunting): Because the lines that need the most throttling to heal the grid are the exact same lines carrying the most dangerous physical stress, PINR automatically narrows the search for catastrophic multi-line failures from 235 lines down to just 27. This cuts the number of three-line failure combinations to check by 99.86% (from over 2.1 million down to under 3,000). Most importantly, testing PINR on the 2026 Western Energy Imbalance Market (WEIM) proves that looking at a static map of the grid is dangerously misleading. While standard map-based analysis points to California's central grid hub (CAISO) as the most critical choke point, PINR's physics engine reveals that California's many parallel lines easily absorb the load. Instead, the true physical bottlenecks hide in the power-exporting corridors of the Desert Southwest (Arizona and the Lower Colorado River) and the mountain seams connecting Montana, the Pacific Northwest, and Utah. Correspondence and collaboration inquiries: aes@acm.org

items.summary: Optimal control of partially observable Markov decision processes (POMDPs), in general, requires a complete history. The belief state, a distribution over hidden states, summarizes this history and provides the classical sufficient statistic to control POMDPs. However, the continuous nature of the belief space generally prevents a finite-memory controller from maintaining it exactly. This raises the question we address in this work: what must the available finite memory preserve to achieve near-optimal control performance? We study this question through an information-theoretic converse that gives a fundamental lower bound on the loss of any finite-memory controller. The analysis introduces the concept of a decision witness that characterizes belief states whose confusion would lead to unavoidable loss. Motivated by this bound, we propose RECAP, a constructive quantization method for designing representative memory states. We prove an upper bound on the optimality gap of any RECAP codebook and use the components of this bound together with the converse analysis to define the codebook objective. Experiments on 11 POMDP benchmarks demonstrate that RECAP improves over finite-memory representation baselines under the same memory budget.
items.title: Finite-Memory Control of POMDPs: Fundamental Limits and Efficient Design

items.summary: Zeroth-order (ZO) optimization has emerged as a promising approach for memory-efficient large language model (LLM) post-training, yet its reliable application to reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) remains largely unexplored. Motivated by the distinct data regimes of on-policy RL and fixed-data optimization, we develop a generic variance-theoretic framework to investigate what limits the reliability of ZO gradient estimation. Our analysis reveals that estimation reliability is structurally determined by whether the two finite-difference evaluations are performed on matched data. On-policy reinforcement learning (RL) under the mismatched-data regime produces a $1/μ^2$ oracle-noise amplification that sets an irreducible noise floor as the perturbation scale $μ$ decreases, whereas Boltzmann Targeted SFT (BOLT) under the matched-data regime eliminates this amplification via noise cancellation. We further derive convergence guarantees with explicit constants that cleanly separate the two regimes. These results naturally lead to ZO-BOLT, which applies ZO optimization to BOLT's RLVR-aligned weighted-SFT objective. Controlled perturbation-scale sweeps and matched-versus-mismatched end-to-end comparisons validate the predicted effect of data matching. Experiments across three model variants and two mathematical reasoning benchmarks further show that ZO-BOLT consistently improves over the pretrained baseline while retaining a near-inference memory footprint. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/lianmin-chen/the_cost_of_mismatch.
items.title: The Cost of Mismatch: Noise Amplification in Zeroth-Order Reinforcement Learning

items.summary: Visual mental imagery (VMI) decoding uses brain activity to reconstruct internally generated visual scenes, providing a potential pathway for externalizing internal experiences and developing neuroprosthetic communication interfaces. However, progress is limited by the lack of dedicated, training-scale VMI datasets. Current VMI paradigms often rely on visual prompts or short-term memory images, introducing visual and mnemonic confounds that make it difficult to disentangle neural activity associated with endogenous image construction from signals driven by prior or concurrent visual input. Furthermore, existing VMI datasets offer limited descriptive control over individual visual attributes, making it difficult to systematically assess fine grained visual details. To address these gaps, we introduce AVID, the first dedicated training-scale 5.0 Tesla functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) resource for auditory-induced VMI decoding. AVID comprises approximately 67 hours of dense recordings from nine participants. The dataset is structured into two complementary splits: a scene-level complex split using naturalistic Mandarin descriptions and a controlled simple split with explicitly specified visual attributes. We further formalize a standardized evaluation protocol that decouples source-image consistency from semantic alignment, allowing for a more nuanced assessment of imagery reconstruction. Baseline qualitative and quantitative results show that current reconstruction pipelines remain limited on AVID, although the most successful reconstructions preserve recognizable scene level semantics from spoken descriptions. By combining dedicated training-scale neural recordings and standardized evaluation resources, AVID provides both a data foundation for imagery-specific model development and a benchmark for evaluating VMI decoding with substantially reduced sensory contamination.
items.title: AVID: A 5T fMRI Dataset for Benchmarking Auditory-induced Visual Mental Imagery Decoding

items.summary: The Sundarbans mangrove system constitutes a globally consequential blue carbon sink, yet vertically resolved soil organic carbon (SOC) inventories, particularly at depth, remain under-constrained. This study deployed a geospatial deep-learning pipeline integrating multi-source Earth observation data (optical, SAR, and DEM-derived covariates) to spatially upscale SOC stocks to 1 m depth across the Bangladesh Sundarbans. Stratified coring across five sites positioned along the salinity–tidal inundation gradient to represent four major vegetation zones (n = 25; one pit per site × five depth intervals: 0–20, 20–40, 40–60, 60–80, 80–100 cm) captured physicochemical and SOC attributions. A Kruskal–Wallis test confirmed a positive SOC gradient with depth (H = 21.7, df = 4, p < 0.001); post-hoc Dunn’s pairwise comparisons showed 60–100 cm layers differed significantly from all shallower layers (p < 0.01, Bonferroni-adjusted), with the dominant pool residing below 40 cm, implying systematic underestimation by conventional shallow-core (<30–40 cm) assessments. To partition total ecosystem carbon and establish soil-pool dominance, above- and belowground biomass were parameterized using species-specific allometric equations, revealing high stem density but comparatively low basal area consistent with a regenerating stand structure dominated by Heritiera fomes and Sonneratia apetala. Analysis of a previously published Landsat-derived mangrove record (1988–2022) revealed net contraction in mangrove extent; loss-agent raster attribution, based on shoreline-proximity buffers, land-cover transition sequences and cyclone-track coincidence, identified chronic tidal abrasion and erosion as the primary driver rather than anthropogenic conversion or cyclonic disturbance. Benchmarking against a previously published global 30 m machine-learning SOC product revealed a 4.2-fold underestimation of SOC stocks in the Bangladesh Sundarbans, particularly in peat-enriched, anoxic substrata. Assimilation of deep-profile in situ observations with the pipeline significantly improves spatial prediction fidelity and establishes a robust baseline for Measurement, Reporting, and Verification for greenhouse gas inventories, highlighting the necessity of incorporating deep-soil carbon pools for inventorizing erosion-vulnerable seaward margins.
items.title: Blue Carbon Stock Mapping of the Sundarbans Mangrove Ecosystem, Bangladesh (2000–2025): A Hybrid GeoAI Ensemble Framework

items.summary: Version 1.02, 3 November 2026. Acemoglu and Restrepo (2020) estimate that one additional industrial robot per thousand workers lowers a U.S. local labor market's employment-to-population ratio by 0.39 percentage points and its hourly wages by about 0.77 percent. Rebuilding their design from raw IPUMS, IFR, and EU KLEMS data, I reproduce these estimates bit-exactly. I then ask what conventional robustness checks leave open: which industries, places, periods, and shocks actually identify the estimate? The regression spans 722 commuting zones and 19 industries, but the variation behind an instrumental-variable estimate can be far narrower. The sign is robust; the support is narrow. Negative estimates persist across conventional specification changes, 60 strong European instrument windows, alternative U.S. treatment windows, and the published periods through 2014. Yet automotive carries about 84 percent of normalized absolute Rotemberg-weight mass, and automotive exposure in six Rust Belt states supplies 95 percent of the net first-stage covariance. Without automotive, the remaining 18 industry shocks do not strongly predict U.S. robot exposure. Longer horizons, later start years, and adding Germany to the instrument all strengthen it through the same margin. The automotive component shows no detectable relation to 1970–1990 employment and wage changes, and a direct effect of the instrument would have to absorb 72 percent of the reduced form before conventional significance disappears. Inference is weaker than the regional first stage suggests. With 19 underlying industry shocks, exposure-robust first-stage F-statistics are 6.2 and 6.3 rather than 34, small-sample Anderson–Rubin tests do not reject a zero effect ( p = 0.059, 0.063), and other implementations of the same test disagree; in known-truth simulations, nominal 95-percent state-clustered intervals cover in only 60–66 percent of replications. Measurement assumptions also bind. In the original penetration metric, perpetual-inventory robot capital preserves the estimates at 5 percent depreciation, but faster assumed depreciation counts the automotive installations behind the first stage as replacement rather than net additions, eliminating shock-level relevance at 10 percent and all relevance at 15 percent. The benchmark is reproducible and robust in sign, but it is identified from an automotive margin in historically industrial labor markets; that margin defines its scope and the concrete content of its exclusion restriction. More generally, coefficient robustness and breadth of identifying support are distinct properties that shift-share studies should report separately. items.title: Robots and Jobs Revisited: A Bit-Exact Replication, Shift-Share Anatomy, and Capital-Stock Extension of Acemoglu and Restrepo (2020)

items.summary: Replication package for the empirical study "Who Migrates the Schema? An Empirical Study of Database Changes in AI Coding Agent Pull Requests" (submitted to Empirical Software Engineering). The study analyses what AI coding agents (OpenAI Codex, GitHub Copilot, Devin, Cursor, Claude Code, Google Jules) do in the database layer (migrations, DDL, ORM schemas, raw SQL) of GitHub pull requests, and compares them with human pull requests from the same 889 database-bearing repositories and the same period (2024-12-24 to 2025-10-24). The package contains (i) code.zip: the frozen detector specification, mining code, human-baseline collector, independent re-implementation, statistical analysis (Python and R), revision analyses, all output tables and the human-validation labels; (ii) data.zip: sanitised per-PR and per-file derived tables sufficient to re-run the statistical analysis. GitHub person logins are pseudonymised (HMAC-SHA256 with a secret salt); bot and agent accounts are kept because they define the treatment. Patch text, PR titles/bodies and comments are not redistributed; scripts to re-collect them are included. Agent-side tables derive from the AIDev dataset (hao-li/AIDev, MSR '26; CC BY 4.0).

items.summary: Progress in robot learning, particularly physical multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL), is currently challenged by a limited availability of accessible, standardized benchmarks. While simulation-based MARL has produced remarkable emergent behaviors, from coordinated team play to complex tool use, translating these advances to physical systems remains difficult. A key barrier is infrastructural: physical platforms are often prohibitively expensive, require specialized facilities, or lack open mechanisms and designs for reproducibility. We introduce KlaskTron, an open-source, low-cost (<\$2500 USD), desktop-scale robotic testbed for adversarial MARL based on the dynamic tabletop game KLASK. The platform features dual CoreXY gantries with high-torque brushless motors, enabling the high-speed, precise manipulation required for competitive play. Crucially, we provide a complete ecosystem: hardware designs (CAD, BOM), a GPU-native digital twin in NVIDIA Isaac Lab for high-fidelity modeling and simulation, and a validated sim-to-real baseline using a learned neural actuator model. We demonstrate that this baseline enables zero-shot policy transfer, with trained agents exhibiting emergent adversarial behaviors. To ensure full reproducibility of our results, all project assets are released publicly: hardware CAD/BOM and assembly documentation at [https://idscethzurich.github.io/klask_hardware], inference software stack at [https://github.com/IDSCETHZurich/klask_software] and the simulation and MARL setup at [https://github.com/IDSCETHZurich/klask_rl].
items.title: KlaskTron: An Open-Source Platform for Physical Adversarial Multi-Agent RL

items.summary: This repository contains the code and numerical data supporting the manuscript “Higher-Order Relational Assurance for Modular Autonomous System Architectures” by Juan J. Segura. The study investigates how much relational information modular system interfaces must preserve in order to reconstruct an integrated dynamic-admissibility relation. The reproducibility package contains Python source code, benchmark configuration files, and CSV datasets and outputs used for the principal computational analyses. The package supports two complementary model layers: (1) a reduced continuous-control model used for exhaustive higher-order project-join analysis and robustness studies, and (2) a synthetic seven-state road-relative vehicle model used as a nonlinear dynamic falsification layer. The principal reproducible results include: complete pairwise reconstruction providing no improvement over unary reconstruction; persistence of this pairwise insufficiency across 27 combinations of numerical resolution, superelevation, and stopping horizon; and a sparse ternary architecture comprising the relations {R, mu, v}, {G, mu, v}, and {mu, v, tau} reproducing the complete third-order reconstruction in all 27 robustness cases. The vehicle parameters are synthetic and are not presented as OEM-calibrated haul-truck data. All admissibility projections are exact only with respect to the computed model relation. The reported discordance measures should not be interpreted as accident probabilities or empirical risk frequencies.
items.title: Code and Data for Higher-Order Relational Assurance for Modular Autonomous System Architectures

items.summary: Long-horizon tasks require large language model (LLM) agents to coordinate interdependent actions, a capability central to automating complex workflows. Stepwise group-based reinforcement learning provides finer credit than trajectory-level supervision, but reliable comparisons must account for differences in interaction history. Enforcing this consistency within the limited rollouts of each task can leave insufficient support for estimating action preferences. We propose Beyond-Local Policy Optimization (BLPO), which estimates task-progress advantages from experience shared across tasks and training updates. We summarize trajectory prefixes into task-progress states and abstract actions by their function, allowing corresponding decisions from different tasks to contribute to shared estimates. To control bias and noise from heterogeneous tasks, we accumulate context-relative returns in a global memory with balanced aggregation and reliability weighting. These global advantages complement local comparisons over normalized actions and trajectory-level credit without a learned critic or additional rollouts. Experiments on ALFWorld and WebShop with 1.5B and 7B policies show improved task success over the evaluated baselines under matched training budgets. Further analyses show faster learning and shorter trajectories with little computational overhead.
items.title: BLPO: Beyond-Local Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
